cases.title: Fake bank anti-fraud adviser asks for confirmations
cases.narrative: A caller, or a text that prompts a call back, presents as the victim's bank anti-fraud adviser and says suspicious transactions are under way. The victim is asked to read out SMS codes or confirm operations in the banking app, which lets the caller approve a new payee and transfers. The caller says the money must be protected and blocked urgently.
cases.source_name: Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr - fiche reflexe, fraude au faux conseiller bancaire

cases.title: Caller says savings must move to a protected account
cases.narrative: A caller claims to be from the bank's fraud department and says the account shows fraud or criminal activity. They offer to protect the money by moving it out of the bank, investment or retirement account, and push the victim to do so.
cases.source_name: FTC Consumer Advice - Never move your money to protect it

cases.title: Phantom hacker: move savings to a government safe account
cases.narrative: A fake tech support representative tells the victim their computer is hacked and asks them to open their financial accounts. A caller then poses as the bank and says a foreign hacker has entered the account, so the savings must be moved immediately to a safe account at a government body. The victim is told not to tell anyone the real reason.
cases.source_name: FBI Little Rock - The Phantom Hacker warning

cases.title: Fake sheriff says a parcel holds drugs or money
cases.narrative: A caller using fake caller ID says they are a sheriff or deputy from the local police department. They claim a package in the victim's name contains money, drugs or weapons, and that the victim will be arrested unless they pay a fine. They press for cash, a Bitcoin ATM deposit, gift card numbers or a payment app transfer.
cases.source_name: FTC Consumer Alert - Scammers are impersonating local law enforcement

cases.title: Urgent trademark payment from the patent office
cases.narrative: An urgent call, text or email seems to come from the US Patent and Trademark Office. It says a trademark must be paid for at once, or someone else will register it first, and asks for payment by card, wire, payment app or gift card.
cases.source_name: FTC Consumer Alert - Scammers are impersonating the United States Patent and Trademark Office

cases.title: Caller posing as FTC official alleges money laundering
cases.narrative: A caller claims to be a senior official of the Federal Trade Commission and says the victim is under investigation for money laundering. To resolve the matter, the victim is told to deposit money at a Bitcoin ATM.
cases.source_name: FTC Consumer Alert - Scammers are impersonating FTC Chief Privacy Officer John Krebs

cases.title: Jailed grandchild and fake lawyer ask for bail
cases.narrative: A caller pretends to be the victim's grandchild, supposedly jailed after a car accident. A second caller, posing as the grandchild's lawyer, asks for legal fees, bail or medical costs, and presses for payment by wire transfer. The victim is told to keep it secret, citing a gag order.
cases.source_name: FBI IC3 PSA - Scammers targeting senior citizens in grandparent scams demanding funds by wire, mail or couriers (2023)

cases.title: Hi Mum text from a new number
cases.narrative: A text arrives from an unknown number starting with Hi Mum. The sender claims they lost their phone, which is why this is a new number, and then asks for money and wants a quick reply.
cases.source_name: ANZ - Hi Mum, it's me (your devoted scammer)

cases.title: Online partner invents an urgent need for money
cases.narrative: Someone met on a dating app or social site builds a relationship through frequent messages and says they live or work far away. They then invent an urgent need, such as medical bills or a plane ticket, and ask for money by a method that is hard to reverse.
cases.source_name: FTC Consumer Advice - What to know about romance scams

cases.title: Online partner directs investing on fake platforms
cases.narrative: An online partner the victim has never met in person keeps making excuses to avoid meeting. They ask for money, gift cards or crypto, give directions for investing on specific online platforms, and ask the victim to receive and send money on their behalf.
cases.source_name: FBI Sacramento - Don't let a romance scammer steal your heart and savings

cases.title: Overseas partner asks for a legal fee
cases.narrative: A romance scammer targets the victim on social media and claims to be travelling or working overseas. After building trust, they ask for money for a medical emergency or an unexpected legal fee.
cases.source_name: FBI Jacksonville - Beware of romance scammers looking for more than love

cases.title: Fake investment manager on a fake trading site
cases.narrative: Contact starts on social media or a dating app, or with an unexpected message. A fake investment manager promises large returns with little or no risk, steers the victim to a convincing fake trading site, and tells them to turn cash into crypto and send it to an account the scammer controls.
cases.source_name: FTC Consumer Advice - What to know about cryptocurrency scams

cases.title: Friend recommends a high-return investment in a group
cases.narrative: A friend or a member of a community group the victim belongs to recommends an investment in forex, stocks or crypto. It is promised as high return with little or no risk, and the victim is shown fake signs of gains.
cases.source_name: FTC Consumer Alert - When investment fraud happens in familiar places

cases.title: Crypto trading website with fabricated returns
cases.narrative: The victim finds a crypto trading website and sees testimonials, rising account screenshots and promises of guaranteed high returns. The returns shown are fabricated, and the victim is asked to deposit money to fund a trading account.
cases.source_name: Investor.gov (SEC) - Digital asset and crypto investment scams investor alert

cases.title: Builder's new bank details on the next invoice
cases.narrative: Someone impersonates a builder or supplier the victim already pays, by sending an altered invoice or by phoning or emailing as that supplier. They say the bank details have changed, and the victim is asked to pay the next bill into the new account.
cases.source_name: Take Five to Stop Fraud - Invoice and mandate fraud (business)

cases.title: Solicitor's account changed before the house deposit
cases.narrative: Criminals who have got into a solicitor's email gather details for weeks, then send a message saying the firm's bank details have changed. The buyer is asked to send the house deposit to the new account, which the criminals control.
cases.source_name: Take Five to Stop Fraud - Conveyancing scams

cases.title: Fake creditor sends a new RIB
cases.narrative: A message appears to come from a creditor the victim deals with, using that creditor's identity to send new bank details (a RIB). If the victim makes the transfer, the money goes to a bank account held by a fraudster.
cases.source_name: Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr - fiche reflexe, que faire en cas de fraude au virement ou faux RIB

cases.title: Pet advertised at a low price never arrives
cases.narrative: An online ad offers a pet at a low price. The seller cannot confirm the animal through a video call or a visit and asks for extra money for various reasons. After the buyer sends the funds, the pet never arrives.
cases.source_name: FBI IC3 PSA - Holiday online shopping and sellers warning (2023)

cases.title: Seller asks for payment to a different person abroad
cases.narrative: A seller posts an item under one name but asks for the money to go to another person. They claim to be inside the buyer's country while asking for the funds to be sent to another country.
cases.source_name: FBI IC3 PSA - Holiday online shopping and sellers warning (2023)

cases.title: Pop-up or call says the computer is infected
cases.narrative: A pop-up, or a call or text from someone posing as a technician for a well-known company, says the victim's computer has a virus. The caller asks for remote access, pretends to scan the computer, and asks for payment by gift card, wire, bank transfer, crypto or payment app to remove the supposed problem.
cases.source_name: FTC Consumer Advice - How to spot, avoid and report tech support scams

cases.title: Urgent Microsoft or Apple pop-up with a phone number
cases.narrative: A pop-up claims to be from Microsoft, Apple or Geek Squad, says the computer has a problem, urges the victim to click right away, and gives a phone number. The caller says the device is infected and sells a bogus service.
cases.source_name: FTC Consumer Alert - Seemingly urgent security messages could lead to tech support scams

cases.title: Caller claims to be a Microsoft technician
cases.narrative: A caller says they are a Microsoft technician and that the victim's computer has viruses. They ask for control of the computer and payment for services the victim does not need.
cases.source_name: FTC Consumer Alert - Hang up on tech support calls

cases.title: Plumber she phoned herself
cases.narrative: A pipe bursts and she searches online for a local plumber. She phones a firm she picked herself and agrees a call-out fee. The plumber's account details are on the invoice he emails her to pay.
cases.source_name: constructed

cases.title: Deposit for a holiday cottage she found herself
cases.narrative: She finds a holiday cottage on a rental site and emails the owner, who runs a small letting business. The owner replies with a booking form and asks for a deposit to a bank account in the business name.
cases.source_name: constructed

cases.title: Gift to grandson's new account after meeting
cases.narrative: Her grandson opened a new bank account last month. She met him in person for lunch, and he showed her the account details on his phone. She now sends a birthday gift to that new account.
cases.source_name: constructed

cases.title: Annual local walking club membership
cases.narrative: She saw the notice of a local walking club and phoned the secretary herself. After two sessions she is paying the annual membership fee to the club account shown on its registration form.
cases.source_name: constructed

cases.title: Gutter firm she pays changed bank, told by post
cases.narrative: A small gutter-cleaning firm she has used for years writes to her by post to say its bank account has changed. She phones the number on an old invoice, not the number in the letter, and the office confirms the change before she pays.
cases.source_name: constructed

cases.title: Used sofa from a marketplace seller, pay tonight
cases.narrative: She bought a used sofa from a private seller she messaged on a marketplace app. She collected it in person and checked it. The seller now asks her to pay by bank transfer this evening because another buyer is interested.
cases.source_name: constructed

cases.title: Electrician after a power cut
cases.narrative: After a power cut trips the fuse box she phones an electrician she found on a registered trade directory. She agrees a visit and pays the deposit by transfer to the account on his written quote.
cases.source_name: constructed

cases.title: Home-care agency for three mornings a week
cases.narrative: She chose a home-care agency after visiting its office and reading its inspection report. She pays the first month's invoice by bank transfer to the agency account listed on it.
cases.source_name: constructed

cases.title: Friend's account for a shared holiday deposit
cases.narrative: A close friend is organising a shared holiday and needs a deposit from each guest. She asked for the account details face to face over coffee, and her friend wrote them on a card. She now pays her share.
cases.source_name: constructed

cases.title: Heating engineer from a registered list
cases.narrative: Her boiler needs a service. She picked a heating engineer from the official register of approved engineers and phoned him herself. He quoted a service fee and asks her to pay by transfer to the account on his quote.
cases.source_name: constructed
